title: Morning Digest, Saturday 28 November 2026
intro: The Centre Party's council meets tomorrow with its leader's job reportedly on the line, a drone strike in Kuwait kills two Italian technicians, eurozone governments pick Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos to run the ECB, and OpenAI countersues Apple.

items.title: Drone strike in Kuwait kills two Italian defence technicians
items.body: Two Rheinmetall Italia employees servicing an air-defence radar site died on Thursday and two other workers were injured. Kuwait and Italy blame Iran, and Rome says the drone was Iranian-made; Tehran calls it a false-flag operation and offers to help trace its origin, while indirect US-Iran talks remain stalled.
items.source: Al Jazeera, 27 Nov; 10 Things (AP, Reuters), 27 Nov

items.title: Eurozone picks Hernández de Cos to lead the ECB
items.body: Finance ministers recommended the former Bank of Spain governor, now head of the Bank for International Settlements, to succeed Christine Lagarde, who leaves on 7 February; he would be the first Spaniard in the post. France's Laurence Boone and Germany's Markus Brunnermeier were put forward for the executive board, and EU leaders are expected to make the formal appointment in December after consulting Parliament.

items.title: Trading partners reject Washington's case for new tariffs
items.body: China, Japan, the EU, Singapore and Malaysia disputed the US finding of excess manufacturing capacity that underpins planned duties on 14 economies, a move to restore tariffs the Supreme Court struck down in February. China faces 20 percent, possibly doubling to 40, and reserves the right to retaliate; the current US-China truce runs to 10 January.

items.title: Wall Street has its best week since spring 2025
items.body: The S&P 500 rose about 5.6 percent over the holiday-shortened week and the Nasdaq about 6.7 percent. Anthropic's shares jumped 11 percent on Friday, their best day since listing on 19 November.

items.title: Trump says he can end the Iran war whenever he wants
items.body: He also warned he could strike Iran's underground nuclear site again; Iran vowed to break the US naval blockade and threatened action at sea and in the air.

items.title: Hamas weighs a response to continued Israeli strikes
items.body: Its leader Khalil al-Hayya said the group would consult other factions, a rare hint of retaliation, after strikes killed at least ten people including a Hamas politburo member. Israel now holds about two-thirds of Gaza, up from just over half when the ceasefire began.

items.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 12,000 confirmed cases
items.body: Official data show 12,021 cases and 5,904 deaths across 8 of 26 provinces since May; the Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment.

items.title: Centre Party council decides tomorrow, and Thand Ringqvist may go if it says no
items.body: The 59-member förtroenderåd meets on Sunday to approve or reject the leadership's plan to vote Kristersson in on Monday and join an M-C-KD-L minority government. Expressen and SVT report the leader will resign if it says no, and that the party's executive committee had voted 3-2 against her line before Thursday's broader meeting. Birgitta Ohlsson and Muharrem Demirok say they will vote against Kristersson regardless; the leadership expects to win, critics a close vote. S, V and MP say their doors remain open if the council overrules her.
items.source: TV4, SVT Text, 27 Nov; News55 (citing SVT, Expressen), 28 Nov (reported)

items.title: Vattenfall raises grid fees by 5 percent
items.body: About 900,000 households and businesses pay more from next year, which the company attributes to grid investment; Ellevio and Eon have not announced 2027 fees.

items.title: Iraq extradites two suspects wanted in Sweden
items.body: A 20-year-old suspected of recruiting for the Foxtrot network and a 21-year-old linked to a 2024 murder in Skärholmen are being sent back, which prosecutors credit to closer cooperation with Baghdad.

items.title: Scheduled
bullets: Sunday 29 November: Centre Party council decides on the Kristersson government; snap general election in Spain.
Monday 30 November: Riksdag votes on Kristersson as prime minister; appeal verdict in Sarkozy's Libyan campaign-financing case; AWS re:Invent opens in Las Vegas.

Tuesday 1 December: Senate Democrats choose between Schumer and Van Hollen; Sweden's temporary fuel-tax cut expires; Estonia closes its land border with Russia; Jensen Huang begins two days of closed-door House committee interviews.
Thursday 3 December: Huang testifies to the Senate Banking Committee on export controls.
items.source: SVT Text; Faithful Intelligence (AI News), 27 Nov; earlier editions

items.title: OpenAI countersues Apple
items.body: Its complaint, filed Friday in California, accuses Apple of stealing trade secrets, pressuring suppliers both companies use and abusing its market power. It answers Apple's July suit claiming former employees took secrets to OpenAI's hardware team.

items.title: Nvidia reportedly halts server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries
items.body: Server partners were told to pause deliveries to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after new US Commerce rules that require permits for large clusters, even abroad, putting regional data-centre projects at risk; Nvidia has also warned cloud providers they may lose GPU access if they rent to Chinese firms.

items.title: Chinese labs warn the export rules will slow their models
items.body: Moonshot reportedly expects the gap between major releases to stretch from about six months to a year or more if it loses overseas compute, and Zhipu's next flagship, GLM-5.5, may slip into 2027.
items.source: The Neuron, note.com digest (citing Reuters), 27 Nov (reported)

items.title: Tencent open-sources a faster decoding method
items.body: DFly2 drafts several tokens ahead for the main model to check, a form of speculative decoding; Tencent reports up to 81 percent higher throughput on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at long context.

items.title: Research pulse
bullets: Harness design for robot agents (Google with Emory, Ohio State and others): 470,000 simulated rollouts across eight benchmarks show that even frontier models fail when asked to output gripper poses directly, and work best when they hand motion to a trained action model through sub-goals and write checked control code; the combined recipe lifts frozen action models by up to 43 points without retraining (arXiv 2611.34778, alphaXiv).

Drawing doesn't help models think yet (Princeton, Meta): having a vision-language model request a generated helper image before answering lowered accuracy in 106 of 130 pipeline-task pairs, by 3.7 points on average and 21 on small-object search, mostly because the model asked for the wrong picture (arXiv 2611.34935, alphaXiv).

OS-Omni (OS-Copilot team): a 300-task benchmark of long computer-use workflows across six operating systems finds the best agent, Claude Opus 5.5, at 68.5 percent against 77.3 for humans, with frontier models beating people on Linux but trailing by over 25 points on iOS and macOS (arXiv 2611.34232, second on Hugging Face daily papers).
items.source: arXiv via alphaXiv and Hugging Face, 24-25 Nov
